claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is called `SUPERSEDED`.
CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode locks a stage to one execution at a time.
CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode only protects an execution once it's actually running.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a newer execution can overtake an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping it before it starts.

If a CodeBuild pipeline stage runs `pulumi up` and enough commits land while it is busy, a queued execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment rather than colliding with one already in progress.
Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` causes waiting executions to form a queue so each runs in turn rather than a later commit erasing an earlier one.
CodePipeline's `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline.
To use `QUEUED` execution mode, both `executionMode` and `pipelineType` must be set when defining the pipeline.
The AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` command supports setting the pipeline's execution mode and pipeline type.
The AWS CLI's `update-pipeline` command supports setting the pipeline's execution mode and pipeline type.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` Pulumi resource has an `executionMode` input.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` Pulumi resource has a `pipelineType` input.
Configuring a CodeBuild project (or CodePipeline source stage) to trigger on git tag events rather than branch pushes makes promotion a single, traceable Git operation.
Configuring a CodeBuild project (or CodePipeline source stage) to trigger on git tag events rather than branch pushes ensures production never deploys from an untested commit.
CodeBuild projects, CodePipeline pipelines, IAM roles, and Parameter Store entries are themselves AWS resources that can be defined with Pulumi using the AWS provider.
Using Pulumi ESC to broker short-lived cloud credentials avoids storing provider keys as pipeline variables at all.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the deployment lease to only one of them.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once and Pulumi Cloud grants the lease to only one, the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines can prevent concurrent stack deployment conflicts at the source with an exclusive lock check on the environment a deployment job targets.
An Azure Pipelines exclusive lock check is added from an environment's Approvals and checks tab.
In Azure Pipelines, `lockBehavior` is a setting configured on the stage that references the environment with the exclusive lock check.
Azure Pipelines supports a `lockBehavior: sequential` setting on a stage definition alongside a deployment job using the `Pulumi@1` task with `command: up`.
Azure Pipelines' `lockBehavior` setting has a default value of `runLatest`.
With Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run ever acquires the lock.
With Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior: runLatest`, an older run stuck waiting behind the most recently queued run is passed over rather than eventually applied.
Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior: sequential` runs every queued stage against the lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud itself serializes updates to a stack one at a time, in order.
The Azure DevOps provider's `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource can be used to manage an Azure Pipelines exclusive lock check as code.
Azure DevOps itself — projects, repositories, pipelines, and service connections — can be managed as code with the Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry.
Pulumi offers native version control integrations for popular Git hosts, independent of TeamCity.
When a Pulumi version control integration is configured, Pulumi Cloud posts infrastructure-change summaries as pull request comments.
When a Pulumi version control integration is configured, Pulumi Cloud posts status checks for infrastructure changes.
When a Pulumi version control integration is configured, Pulumi Cloud links each stack update back to the commit and pull request that produced it.
If two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When Pulumi Cloud grants the stack update lease to only one of two concurrent runs, the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
TeamCity's own default behavior is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as it has.
TeamCity does not, by default, stop two concurrent runs of the same build configuration from racing to reach the same stack.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option called 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' located under that configuration's General Settings.
The TeamCity build configuration option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' defaults to 0, meaning unlimited concurrent builds.
Setting the TeamCity 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option to 1 causes a second build that would otherwise start immediately to be queued behind the first build instead.
When the TeamCity 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option is set to 1, a queued second build runs only once the first build finishes.

Setting TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option to 1 gives the same one-at-a-time behavior as Pulumi Cloud's own per-stack lease, but applied earlier so the build never gets far enough to hit the update conflict.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment a deployment job targets, with `lockBehavior: sequential` set on the stage, serializes deployments.
Azure Pipelines supports a `lockBehavior: sequential` setting on a pipeline stage.
Azure Pipelines supports adding an exclusive lock check to an environment that a deployment job targets.
AWS CodePipeline has a pipeline-level setting called execution mode that can be set to `QUEUED` so that waiting executions run in turn.
AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode lets a newer pipeline execution supersede an older execution that is still waiting to start.
Setting AWS CodePipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` causes waiting executions to run in turn instead of allowing a newer execution to supersede an older waiting one.
In TeamCity, setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to `1` on the build configuration serializes deployment builds.
TeamCity has a build configuration setting called 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds'.
